title: IMIE intelligent retina restores partial vision to a blind woman at Xiangya Hospital
summary: Blind over a decade, a 61-year-old woman read E optotypes and walked indoors unaided after a 256-channel IMIE retinal implant in Changsha.
account: On 23 April 2026 Prof. Xu Huizhuo's team implanted the IMIE intelligent retina in a 61-year-old woman known as Auntie Chen. The team is at Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, Changsha. The implant is a 256-channel epiretinal array driven by camera glasses and an external video processor. She was diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa at 40 and had been blind for over ten years. Mark Humayun advised in theater, and no serious complications occurred. On 5 June 2026 the hospital announced that after over a month of rehabilitation she could identify E optotypes (acuity 0.03, peak 0.1). She could also walk indoors and through doorways without an escort. She is the first subject of a Phase I trial. The team says she lacks full self-care ability and will be observed for a year.
purpose: Built to restore partial sight to people blinded by photoreceptor degeneration by converting camera images into electrical stimulation of surviving retinal ganglion cells. The benefit recorded here is exactly that intended function.
system: IMIE intelligent retina (IMIE智能视网膜): 256-channel flexible epiretinal electrode array fixed on the macula, with camera glasses and an external video processing unit transmitting wirelessly to the implant
model_version: 256-channel array; the device lineage is the IMIE 256 (Intelligent Micro Implant Eye, also called Theia α) reported in TVST 2021
developer: Xiangya Hospital (Prof. Xu Huizhuo's team, per 2026 reports, which name no company); the IMIE 256 was co-developed by Golden Eye Bionics LLC (Pasadena) and IntelliMicro Medical Co., Ltd. (Changsha) and manufactured by IntelliMicro, per Xu et al. 2021
deployer: Xiangya Hospital, Central South University (Ophthalmology Center), in a Phase I clinical trial led by Prof. Xu Huizhuo

ratings.reason: One identifiable person, totally blind for more than ten years, regained enough vision to identify E optotypes (0.03, peak 0.1). She can walk indoors and through doorways without an escort. The hospital cautions that she does not yet have full self-care ability and needs long-term rehabilitation.

ai_role.statement: The system is the whole substitute visual pathway. Camera glasses capture the scene. An external processor converts each frame in real time into stimulation patterns across 256 electrodes. The implant stimulates surviving ganglion cells whose signals reach the visual cortex. The patient had no vision before, so the benefit is attributable to the system together with structured rehabilitation. The 2026 reports describe the conversion only as an algorithm inside an “intelligent” retina. The 2021 IMIE 256 paper describes a video processing unit with a per-electrode threshold map and 15 gray levels and no learned model. How much of that processing is AI in a machine-learning sense is not established by these sources.

fields.account: On 23 April 2026 Prof. Xu Huizhuo's team implanted the IMIE intelligent retina in a 61-year-old woman known as Auntie Chen. The team is at Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, Changsha. The implant is a 256-channel epiretinal array driven by camera glasses and an external video processor. She was diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa at 40 and had been blind for over ten years. Mark Humayun advised in theater, and no serious complications occurred. On 5 June 2026 the hospital announced that after over a month of rehabilitation she could identify E optotypes (acuity 0.03, peak 0.1). She could also walk indoors and through doorways without an escort. She is the first subject of a Phase I trial. The team says she lacks full self-care ability and will be observed for a year.

fields.summary: Blind over a decade, a 61-year-old woman read E optotypes and walked indoors unaided after a 256-channel IMIE retinal implant in Changsha.
fields.account: On 23 April 2026 Prof. Xu Huizhuo's team implanted the IMIE intelligent retina in a 61-year-old woman known as Auntie Chen. The team is at Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, Changsha. The implant is a 256-channel epiretinal array driven by camera glasses and an external video processor. She was diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa at 40 and had been blind for over ten years. Mark Humayun advised in theater, and no serious complications occurred. On 5 June 2026 the hospital announced that after over a month of rehabilitation she could identify E optotypes (acuity 0.03, peak 0.1). She could also walk indoors and through doorways without an escort. She is the first subject of a Phase I trial. The team says she lacks full self-care ability and will be observed for a year.
